Every School on the Map

An open database of the world's schools, built to protect children. If one civilian can map them, any military can avoid them.

1 Without school location data
● Clear — no known civilian infrastructure
2 With school location data
◆ Warning — school identified within blast radius

The difference between these two frames is one dataset. School locations are public knowledge. OpenStreetMap alone contains hundreds of thousands of them, mapped by volunteers worldwide. Integrating this data into military planning is not a technical challenge — it is a decision.

Built with open data from OpenStreetMap. This is a civilian project demonstrating that the data exists and is usable. The only missing ingredient is the will to use it.

Why does this exist?

International humanitarian law requires parties to a conflict to distinguish between civilian objects and military objectives. Schools are civilian objects. Their locations are knowable — and in many cases, already mapped.

This tool draws from publicly available, open data to plot schools across conflict-affected countries. One civilian built it. One person, with a laptop, using free tools and open data.

If one person can build this with public data, there is no excuse for any military power not to have — and use — a comprehensive database of school locations to protect children.

The data is there. The technology is there. What remains is to use it.
